stories.title: Suzuki QO Incoming — Formal Farewell Begins
stories.angle: Jon Heyman: Cubs expected to extend $23.15M QO to Suzuki. He will decline. Five seasons, career-best 2026 (.270/.368/.473, 26 HR). Blue Jays lead suitors. Market projected at $100M+. QO comes 5 days after WS ends.

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text:
FIVE SEASONS. 26 homers. .270/.368/.473 in 2026.

Jon Heyman: Cubs expected to extend Seiya Suzuki a $23.15M qualifying offer.

He'll decline it. The Blue Jays are waiting. The market will pay him $100M+.

Thank you, Seiya.

#Cubs #MLB #CubsBaseball

research.facts:
Suzuki QO Incoming
**Decision:** NEW STORY (QO news is fresh per Heyman report. Oct 9 story was about Blue Jays interest/speculation. Today's angle is the QO itself being imminent — a different hook.)
**Sources:**
1. Bleacher Nation (Oct 2026) — Heyman report embedded: "Cubs expected to make him a qualifying offer" — MEDIUM confidence (industry reporting, not official Cubs statement yet)
2. Bleacher Nation, Oct 8, 2026: "The qualifying offer number for post-2026 free agents is out" — $23.15M confirmed — HIGH confidence (corroborated Joel Sherman/NY Post)
3. Spotrac player page (Suzuki contract): Final year of 5-year/$85M, 2026 — HIGH
4. Baseball Reference (via research) — 2026 stats: .270/.368/.473, 26 HR, 5.1 WAR — MEDIUM (web summary, not directly verified from BBRef page)
5. The Athletic's Mitch Bannon (via Bleacher Nation Oct 2): Blue Jays expected to pursue — MEDIUM
**Key Facts:**
- QO = $23.15M one-year offer (5th straight year rising ~$1M)
- Suzuki 2026: .270 BA, .368 OBP, .473 SLG, 26 HR, 5.1 WAR (career-best)
- Age: 32 (born January 18, 1994 — verify for any age claims)
- Final year of 5-year/$85M deal
- Cubs "unlikely to win a bidding war" (Bleacher Nation)
- Blue Jays lead suitors
- QO timeline: 5 days after World Series ends (WS hasn't started; ALCS ongoing)
**Fact-Check Flags:**
- Do NOT cite Suzuki's exact age in tweet without BBRef verification
- "5.1 WAR" is from AI-summarized web result — MEDIUM confidence. Do not claim as superlative
- "Career-best" WAR — plausible given earlier WAR totals, but not cross-referenced. Flag.
**Why It Matters:**
Suzuki has been a cornerstone of the Cubs' outfield for 5 years. This is the beginning of the formal goodbye process. Cubs fans know they're losing him — this makes it official and quantifies his value one more time before he walks.

stories.title: Michael King Countdown — Cubs' Must-Have FA
stories.angle: WS starts imminently; King opt-out deadline 5 days after WS. Skubal gone. King (3.23 ERA, 2026) is the best arm on the market. Cubs need 4 starters. Horton TJ. This is the move of the offseason.

x_posts.text:
FOUR starters needed. Horton out until mid-2027. Gausman, Holmes, Peterson, Imanaga all gone.

Michael King (3.23 ERA, 28) is expected to opt out 5 days after the World Series.

He's the best arm available this winter. The Cubs don't have a Plan B.

#Cubs #MLB #CubsBaseball

research.facts:
Michael King Countdown
**Decision:** FOLLOW UP (Oct 13 story covered King broadly; Oct 15 QO countdown mentioned King timing. Today = fresh angle with WS opponent being finalized imminently, making King's opt-out clock active.)
**Sources:**
1. GaslampBall (Padres blog, Oct 2026): King opts out per MLBPA free agent announcement — note: this may be from prior offseason (pre-re-signing). Treat as LOW confidence for 2026 opt-out confirmation.
2. CBS Sports (via research): King re-signed Padres 3yr/$75M with two player options — HIGH confidence
3. MLB.com opt-out preview (Aug 29, 2026): King's mutual option for 2026/27 — HIGH. "Second-best pitcher on the market" behind Skubal — MEDIUM
4. MLB.com opt-out article: Deadline 5 days after WS — HIGH
**Key Facts:**
- King 2026: 3.23 ERA, 27 starts
- Contract: 3-year/$75M signed after 2025; has player options after '26 and '27
- Deadline: 5 days post-WS (WS starts within days)
- Ranked No. 2 FA this offseason (Skubal No. 1 — but Skubal signed 1-year Dodgers deal per Oct 15 coverage)
- Expected to opt out per multiple reports
- Cubs need: 4 rotation spots open (Gausman, Holmes, Peterson, Imanaga all FA; Boyd mutual option unlikely; Horton TJ out until mid-2027)
- Sonny Gray was one target (covered Oct 14)
**Fact-Check Flags:**
- King's ERA "3.23" — from MLB.com opt-out preview (Aug 2026 data), not season-final stats. Note as approximate.

- Do NOT state King "will opt out" — say "expected to"

stories.title: Bold Take — Jed Hoyer, Go Get Michael King
stories.angle: Brewers in the World Series. Cubs watching from home. The gap is real but fixable: one elite SP changes everything. Cubs' lineup (PCA, Bregman, Swanson, Busch) is already top-10 NL. One move — King — makes 2027 a real year.

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
THE BREWERS are in the World Series. The Cubs are watching.

The gap is real — and it's fixable. Chicago's lineup is top-10 in the NL. PCA. Bregman. Swanson. Busch.

One move changes this winter: Michael King.

Jed Hoyer, go get him.

#Cubs #GoCubs #MLB

research.facts:
Bold Offseason Take
**Decision:** NEW STORY (synthesis take not directly covered before — framing Cubs' entire winter around one SP acquisition)
**Sources:**
- Pipeline knowledge: Horton TJ (out until mid-2027), Gausman/Holmes/Peterson/Imanaga all FA, Boyd mutual option unlikely to be picked up, Bregman 5yr/$175M signed, PCA/Swanson core in place
- Research: King as No. 2 FA, Skubal gone, Gray targeted (Oct 14)
**Key Facts:**
- 4 of 5 rotation spots open entering winter
- Horton: Tommy John, not back until mid-2027
- Core intact: PCA (45/40, MVP candidate), Bregman (5.8 WAR in 2026), Swanson, Happ (if retained)
- Brewers in WS: direct competitor with a complete roster
- Cubs path: add 1-2 quality SPs, let Alcantara/Hartshorn develop, target King
**Why It Matters:**
The juxtaposition of Brewers in WS vs. Cubs watching from home crystallizes exactly what Chicago needs. Not a teardown moment — a targeted rebuild moment. The pieces are there offensively; the rotation is the only real problem. That makes this winter decisive.
